spec.description: Response payload throughput for this route, and request payload where it is recorded. HEADS UP: http_request_size_bytes_sum only exists for 29 of 198 paths (the app appears to record it only when the request carries a body), while http_response_size_bytes_sum covers all 198. So 'Inbound' is legitimately absent for most routes — that is missing instrumentation, not zero bytes. This same gap affects panels 9 and 35 on CRM-Overview.
spec.title: 📦 Payload In / Out

spec.expr: sum by (host, container) (rate(http_requests_total{path="$route", host=~"$host", container=~"$container", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description: Same route split per host and container — use this to spot a single bad instance.
spec.title: 🖥️ By Host + Container

spec.description: Every trace whose server span matched this route. Click the Trace ID to open the waterfall. Sort by Duration to find the slow tail behind the P99 stat above.
spec.title: 🔍 Traces for $route

spec.description: Access-log lines for this route. NOTE: the access log records the RAW url (/crm/v1/renewal/lead/update/172821), while Prometheus and Tempo record the TEMPLATED route (/crm/v1/renewal/lead/update/:leadID). The $route_prefix variable bridges the two by capturing everything before the first ':'. 195 of 198 routes match exactly. The exceptions are routes whose first ':param' is not the last segment — /crm/services/:serviceHandle/:targetHandle/options/list, its /:currentState/ sibling, and /crm/v1/payment/prospect/:actionName/:orderID — where the prefix is broader than the route and neighbouring routes appear too. Check the parsed 'path' field on each line to tell them apart. Each line also carries trace_id, which you can paste into the Trace Watcher to jump to the waterfall.
